title: Page-mode progress persistence uses raw page offsets instead of visible page starts
symptom: ReaderPageSlice already records both raw page bounds and visible page bounds after trimming leading newlines, but ReaderPageAnchorMapper.anchorForPageIndex returned startCharOffset. In page mode, savePageProgress() and updateReaderSettings() both use that mapper, so a page that renders after trimming leading newlines can persist an anchor before the first visible character. The focused regression failed with a page whose raw start was 100 and visible start was 102.
root_cause: The page slice model was partially migrated to visible/raw offsets, but the shared anchor mapper kept the older raw-start behavior. That left page-top TTS start on the visible offset path while progress persistence and settings-change anchoring still used the raw page start.
fix: Move raw-text to visible-offset ReaderPageSlice construction into a shared helper and use it from both ReaderScreen pagination and ReaderPageLinePaginator.
Add a unit regression where a page trims leading newlines and must persist the visible start offset.
Add a ReaderPageLinePaginator regression so standalone pagination cannot reintroduce raw-start slices when a page begins with leading newlines.
Run adjacent page-mode, settings-persistence, and restore instrumentation tests on the Pixel 8 Android 14 emulator to check that the mapper change does not break existing interaction paths.

2026-09-11: page-to-page navigation still uses visible starts, but layout-only restoration preserves its requested source character inside the rendered page. A device regression exposed character 1207 being replaced by new page start 1166; ReaderPageReflowTest now passes 32→18→32 sp while keeping character 1207. Whitespace gaps map to the following visible page, or the last visible character at chapter end.
failed_attempts: Existing page-mode UI tests without pages that start on trimmed leading newlines are insufficient evidence for this bug; they cover adjacent interactions but cannot prove the raw/visible offset boundary.
Keeping separate ReaderPageSlice construction paths lets an unused or later-reused paginator silently fall back to default raw offsets; centralize raw/visible slice construction instead.
impact: Reduces page-mode restore, setting-change re-anchor, and future TTS-start divergence when a rendered page begins after raw newline characters that are not visible to the reader.
